description: Four signals stretched and shifted to fill a voltage window set by two knobs, working the scaling out from the signal as it arrives

params.text: Sets the bottom of the window the output is made to fill, -10V fully counter-clockwise to +10V fully clockwise, and -5V unless you move it
Sets the top of the window the output is made to fill, -10V fully counter-clockwise to +10V fully clockwise, and +5V unless you move it
Mirrors the Max knob onto the Min knob while it is on, so setting Min to -3V puts Max at +3V
Throws away the scaling worked out so far, so it is rebuilt from what arrives next, and turns the menu lock back off

inputs.text: A rising edge throws away the scaling worked out so far and turns the menu lock back off; it reads high above 1V and low below 0.1V
One of the four signals to be scaled; a light beside it brightens whenever that signal is outside the window and then fades

outputs.text: Carries that input stretched and shifted to fill the window, clamped to it at the ends

notes: the scaling is learnt from the signal, so the first moments after a reset are the range it has seen so far, not the range it will end up with
pulling a cable out of an input throws away that section's scaling on its own, so it starts again when you patch something back
setting Min above Max turns the window inside out and the output is flipped within it, which a small red light beside Min shows
this module has no clipping range on its menu, because the Min and Max knobs already bound every output
menu: Update Scale/offset-values: Disabled (locked), Enabled — locked, the scaling stops being revised and anything beyond the window is clamped instead; a reset unlocks it again
Scale/offset-usage: Individual (per section), Common (all sections) — chooses whether each section works out its own scaling or all four share one
Set min/max-range — sets the two knobs to a named pair, from -1 to +1 up to unipolar 0 to +10, each also offered with the ends swapped for inversion
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
